articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq close higher as tech stocks surged, but the Dow slips as yields rise
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq close higher as tech stocks surged, but the Dow slips as yields rise
articles.content_orig:
This week's major earnings hold the key to whether this technology comeback has legs, investors said.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite rallied Monday, largely due to a rebound in artificial intelligence  companies. Chip stocks surged, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) on pace to snap a nine-day slump. The Magnificent Seven outperformed, as did memory chip makers. The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF ( EWY ), dominated by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, surged 4% after also suffering steep declines over the past week.
That comes after the S&P 500 fell nearly 2% last week, its worst weekly decline since late June. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 4.5% over the same five-day span.
Monday looked like a bounce from oversold conditions, but a bigger move will depend on this week's big tech earnings — which include results from major names such as Meta Platforms and Tesla — to clear some of the recent worries about the sustainability of the AI trade. SpaceX reports after the bell Tuesday.
"Tech earnings are key this week. Fundamentals are unchanged, but given fragile price action, we turn neutral [on] risk assets and stay neutral duration," wrote Ajay Rajadhyaksha, global chairman of research at Barclays.
This week will be especially crucial for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which need to hold support so as not to confirm a further breakdown, Katie Stockton, founder of Fairlead Strategies, said in a Monday note. For the time being, however, widespread, short-term oversold conditions suggest support can hold, she said.
Of the 47 S&P 500 companies that have reported their third quarter thus far, 85% have beaten expectations, and the broad market index is on track to post a blended earnings growth rate of 29%.
But the bulk of tech results are still to come, and they have a high bar to clear.
"Investors are going to need proof statements from any company that is considered part of the AI trade that they can deliver on the earnings growth expectations being built into their pricing," said Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at LNW. "We don't have a valuation-potential bubble here like we had in the internet bubble. We have an earnings-expectation-potential bubble in this cycle."
As a result, the market will take a "more discriminating" approach to tech, which Albahary views as a healthy move that will lead to "more of a dispersion of winners and losers within the AI trade universe." In that environment, some AI beneficiaries may continue to rise, while others like the neocloud platforms may sell off due to the amount of debt they're taking on to finance the build-out, he said.
"Previously, the AI headlines would drive the bulk of the AI universe stocks up or down," the CIO said. "I don't think we're going to see that kind of uniformity going forward."
As it stands now, action in the AI trade appears to be more of a "reality check" than a "full-blown unraveling," according to Wells Fargo Investment Institute's Sameer Samana. But he still believes there may be more pressure in the days and maybe even weeks ahead.
"We recently downgrade[d] tech because we thought expectations had gotten too optimistic, and while the recent selling has taken some of that optimism out of the equation, we don't think it's fully done and may last through the midterms given the politicization of AI/data centers," the Wells Fargo head of global equities and real assets told CNBC.

articles.title_zh: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
articles.content_orig:

On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at the the software advantage that has helped Nvidia become the default hardware choice for AI apps, and spurred its rise as AI hardware provider of choice.
TorchNeuron works with PyTorch, a free, open-source toolkit that developers use to build, train, and run AI models. It lets AI apps written with PyTorch run on Trainium by changing just one line of configuration, according to Amazon — no code rewrite required.
Amazon says about 85% of AI apps are written with PyTorch. Facebook originally developed it, but since 2022, it has been part of the Linux Foundation, which maintains open-source projects. Nvidia has spent years ensuring its CUDA software — the software infrastructure that allows apps to run on Nvidia GPUs and its other hardware — seamlessly supports AI apps written with PyTorch. As a result, Nvidia’s hardware is now deeply embedded in the toolkit, essentially by default.
TorchNeuron is adapted from PyTorch, so developers who know PyTorch already know how to use it. Amazon isn’t the first company to attempt to easily bring their chips to the platform. PyTorch users can also port their apps to AMD GPUs or even Apple’s chips with a simple configuration change.
However, Amazon argues that porting to Trainium isn’t just easy; it also gives AI startups access to Amazon’s entire cloud. Unsurprisingly, AWS claims that this is a better choice for startups than using neoclouds, many of which are tied to Nvidia and its hardware, like Coreweave, Nebius, and Firmus.
“You’re building on AWS. You’re not betting on a single-purpose compute provider and scrambling to build everything else around it,” Colin Brace, VP of Technology Software at AWS Annapurna Labs (the unit that makes Amazon’s custom chips) told TechCrunch via email. “On AWS,” he continued, “the infrastructure to go from prototype to production is already there, allowing a founder to move fast and scale when they need to.”
AWS says that because the same chip both handles training (teaching the AI model) and inference (putting the finished model to work, as when it answers a user’s question), and is tightly integrated with the cloud infrastructure that startups need, its cloud will save them money, even if AWS doesn’t offer the cheapest per-token price.
“Trainium’s value is price-performance plus the fact that it’s one platform for both training and inference, which improves the economics across a full workload,” Brace said. “Look at Deepgram — they moved to Trainium using native PyTorch, support and they’re processing 70% more audio per dollar at production-grade accuracy.” Deepgram is an AI voice app provider, a competitor to ElevenLabs.
But Amazon isn’t content to just give PyTorch app developers an easy option to move to its cloud.
Amazon also says it is pushing PyTorch to be less automatically centered on Nvidia, and it will contribute the code to do that to the main PyTorch project. In the blog post announcing the new tool, the company wrote:
“Amazon’s approach extends beyond its own hardware. The company is contributing changes upstream to PyTorch itself, working with the PyTorch community to remove code that ties the framework to specific chips. The goal is to make PyTorch more hardware-agnostic for the entire developer community, not just Trainium users.”
While such a tactic is undoubtedly good for those who are selling hardware and cloud services that compete with Nvidia, one of the points of PyTorch is to hide all the pesky difficulties of getting AI code to run on hardware. We’ll have to wait and see if pushing Nvidia out that far gives developers more choice and more affordable options, as Amazon promises, or just more configuration headaches.
Either way, if Amazon succeeds in deeply uncoupling PyTorch from Nvidia, this could have much bigger ramifications for the GPU giant than simply dealing with chip competitors. As Brace said: “The real story is removing the lock-in that kept developers from having a real choice at all.”

articles.title_orig: Saudi Arabia executes 2 Bangladeshis over ‘indecent acts,’ and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Saudi Arabia executes 2 Bangladeshis over ‘indecent acts,’ and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
Bangladeshi authorities say they were not informed of the recent execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in the holy city of Mecca until after it had taken place, local media reports.
A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed last Wednesday after being convicted of committing an "indecent act" inside a mosque, according to the Saudi interior ministry. The ministry did not specify the nature of the offending act.
Bangladesh says it has reached out to the Saudi Arabian government to ask for more details about the case.
The two Muslim countries share a close relationship due to their religious affinity and strong economic ties.
More than three million Bangladeshis work and live in Saudi Arabia, mostly in low-paying jobs, and news of the double execution has raised public concern in Bangladesh.
According to the Saudi interior ministry, the two Bangladeshi nationals were convicted and sentenced to death under "tazir", which in Islamic law refers to punishments left to the discretion of the judge.
The ministry statement said they were handed the sentences because of the severity of the offence, and the fact that they violated the "sanctity" of the mosque.
Bangladesh has reached out to the Saudi government about the offences involved and legal proceedings in the case, said state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam.
The government would consider next steps, such as the repatriation of the bodies, after getting information from Saudi authorities, Islam said.
She added that the government was committed to safeguarding the welfare and interests of Bangladeshis abroad.
The two executed Bangladeshis were included in a list of prisoners that Saudi Arabia had shared with Bangladesh, upon a request from the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah - but that list did not indicate that the pair had been sentenced to death, the Daily Star reported.
This is not the first time that foreign nationals have been executed by Saudi authorities.
According to Amnesty International, the country has executed around 100 people this year, many of whom are foreigners convicted of drug offences.
In 2011, eight Bangladeshi men were publicly executed in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh after they were found guilty of killing an Egyptian.
Earlier this month, Saudi Arabia overturned a death sentence handed to a Sri Lankan man over a comment he had made on Facebook, which had led to him being convicted of blasphemy. That decision came after the case sparked public outcry in Sri Lanka and spurred diplomatic efforts to seek clemency for the man.

articles.title_orig: France Imposes Curfews in Parts of Paris and Other Cities After Nationwide Rioting
articles.title_zh: France Imposes Curfews in Parts of Paris and Other Cities After Nationwide Rioting
articles.content_orig:
“We have a mess on our hands, to put it bluntly,” French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Monday.
If anything, he might be guilty of understatement. After widespread rioting at the weekend – estimated to have cost several hundred million dollars in property damage and theft – France faces a toxic mix of urban rebellion, political drift and economic crisis.
The disorder at the weekend occurred in major cities across the country, leading Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to offer his resignation because of the police’s failure to contain the rioting.
There was rampant looting in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and other cities, while the city hall in Limoges, which survived two world wars, was badly damaged by fire and its clock spire collapsed.
The violence at the weekend, which led to some 2,400 arrests, followed weeks of protests by French students angry about crumbling schools, a lack of teachers and dismal job prospects. More than 6,000 arrests were made during the school protests that began at the start of the fall term and more than 100 schools were damaged.
More demonstrations are scheduled for next weekend. In November, labor unions plan to strike.
France faces a winter of discontent in the run-up to a presidential election next spring. The far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is leading in the polls.
In a national televised address Sunday, President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence but did not set out ideas to deal with it or seize the initiative. Instead, he warned of politicians seizing on the chaos for political gain – before leaving France for a three-day visit to the Gulf states.
Lecornu similarly deployed the blame game. After far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon accused the government of “opening the door to chaos” with its policing tactics, Lecornu shot back: “You cannot call for an end to the violence while providing excuses to those who commit it. This is YOUR political responsibility.”
Le Pen, who is standing in the presidential election for the far-right National Rally party, has sought to inject the issue of migration into the debate, blaming the violence on delinquents from France’s banlieues , poor urban areas where much of the country’s migrant population lives.
Buildings torched after protests descend into rioting across France
“Our country is caught in a vice…between violence and powerlessness,” she said, suggesting only her firm hand could restore order amid Macron’s “chaos.”
The president of her National Rally party, Jordan Bardella, poured fuel on the fire, demanding that “Antifa militias, far-left extremist groups and Black Bloc groups” be designated as terrorist organisations.”
Black Bloc groups wear matching or similar black clothing along with face masks during protests to hide their identity.
Analysts say this political fragmentation, which led to the paralysis of parliament after snap elections called by Macron in 2024 backfired, is likely to persist – and is at the core of France’s deepening crisis.
The political center in France has evaporated, allowing the National Rally and Mélenchon’s far-left France Unbowed party to harvest growing public exasperation, while Macron’s successive prime ministers have been unable to pass a budget through Parliament.
The multitude of candidates in the center, “most with relatively few supporters, will ultimately help secure the second-round election for one of the two contenders who represent the greatest danger to democracy in France,” wrote Robert Zaretsky, a professor of modern French history at the University of Houston, in an essay for the Atlantic.
The current crisis has polarized an already deeply divided society. Besides the shock and anger at the weekend’s mayhem, there is an air of defeatism. In a recent Ipsos-BVA poll , 85% of respondents said that France was in decline, and 98% were dissatisfied with the present state of the country.
Whoever governs France next will have shrinking room for maneuver, even if they can stitch together a stable coalition.
The French economy is stagnating. Farmers were hit by an extremely hot and dry summer, while global energy prices stoked inflation.
Tourism remains a strong earner for France, but the videos of violence on the streets circling the globe in the past two days may deter some travelers.
French businesses are wary of the drift and indecision. Investment has fallen about 1% in the first half of this year amid climbing interest rates.
Above all, there is the debt.
“France carries one of the highest government debt burdens in Europe, and political deadlock means we expect its debt level to continue rising,” researchers at Oxford Economics said in July.
France will have to issue a record high of €340 billion in medium- and long-term bonds next year, according to analysts . Its debt as a proportion of gross domestic product (GDP) rose to 119% in the second quarter of this year, double the European Union’s target.
Jittery investors sent the country’s 10-year government bond yield up to 4.9% on Monday.
Its reputation in bond markets is not helped by Mélenchon’s plan to freeze or wipe away the French sovereign bonds held by the Bank of France.
“Political fragmentation may persist well after the 2027 elections, meaning that France’s next government will continue to kick the public-finance can down the road,” said Oxford Economics. This would “prolong the existing climate of high uncertainty, weighing on confidence and domestic demand.”
The man most revered by the French, General Charles de Gaulle, once declared that “France cannot be France without grandeur. ” De Gaulle had soaring ambitions for the country’s global role and independence.
But during his long presidency he also told an aide: “I keep the theater going as long as I can and then, after me, have no illusion, things will go back to where they were.”
De Gaulle stepped down a year after the 1968 riots that shook France – events that some commentators are likening to today’s shock.
When he became president, Macron was seen as the antidote to what the French call déclinisme (a word that first appeared in the French Larousse dictionary in 2016.)
“He delivers an extremely positive, constructive message, full of hope for the future. He shows that there is also another France,” wrote one commentator.
A decade later, Macron’s approval rating is hovering at about 15 to 17%, according to multiple polls Déclinisme is still very much on the lips of a citizenry that is demanding more from a beleaguered state that has less.

articles.title_orig: Homeland Security grants temporary deportation reprieve for more than 100K Ukrainians and Sudanese
articles.title_zh: Homeland Security grants temporary deportation reprieve for more than 100K Ukrainians and Sudanese
articles.content_orig:
Immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan enrolled in the Temporary Protected Status policy will be able to live and work in the U.S. without fear of deportation for the time being, even though their protections were set to expire soon, the Department of Homeland Security told CBS News on Sunday.
The TPS protections of tens of thousands of Ukrainians and hundreds of Sudanese immigrants were officially slated to terminate on Monday.
But in statements on Sunday, DHS said final decisions on the fate of the humanitarian immigration programs will "be made at the appropriate time."
Until such decisions are announced, DHS added, nationals of Ukraine and Sudan enrolled in the TPS program will "retain protection."
The decisions to keep the deportation protections in place, albeit not final, stand in sharp contrast to the Trump administration's broader posture toward TPS programs.
Trump administration officials have routinely denounced TPS as a de facto amnesty policy abused by the Biden administration that encourages illegal immigration and that has been extended too often, despite its temporary nature.
Over the past year and a half, the Trump administration, as part of its aggressive immigration crackdown, has revoked the TPS protections of more than 1 million immigrants from over a dozen countries, including Afghanistan, Haiti and Venezuela.
The programs for Ukrainian and Sudanese nationals are among a handful of TPS policies that have remained in place nearly two years into President Trump's second term, alongside the protections for tens of thousands of immigrants from El Salvador. Their TPS program was also set to lapse last month, but DHS retained their protections, pending a final announcement.
Created in 1990 by Congress, TPS allows the U.S. government to offer a temporary deportation reprieve and work permits to immigrants, illegal and legal alike, who hail from countries facing armed conflict, an environmental disaster or another crisis that makes their return there unsafe.
The TPS policy for Ukrainians was first announced by the Biden administration in the spring of 2022, soon after Russia launched its full-blown invasion of Ukraine. As of March 2025 , there were more than 100,000 Ukrainians enrolled in TPS, including those allowed into the U.S. under a Biden-era sponsorship policy.
The TPS program for Sudan has been around since the late 1990s, with different administrations extending the policy due to the armed conflict and political turmoil that has plagued the African nation. As of March 2025 , roughly 1,800 Sudanese nationals had TPS.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk says he plans to gift a SpaceX share to every child in the U.S.
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk says he plans to gift a SpaceX share to every child in the U.S.
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk said in a social media post on Monday that he plans to give one of his SpaceX shares to each child in the U.S., writing that the gift "will be the first of many."
Musk didn't specify how the shares would be distributed or other details of how the pledge might be fulfilled. The offer arrived a day after artificial intelligence company Anthropic announced that it will commit 5% of its shares to a new "public benefit" fund.
Anthropic said it will contribute an additional 2% of shares at its board's discretion for every 50% increase in the company's value, above a set threshold.
Shares of SpaceX, which will report quarterly earnings on Tuesday, rose $3.46, or 2.7%, to $149.49 in Monday morning trading.
The SpaceX CEO is the company's largest shareholder with a 10.5% stake, according to financial data firm FactSet. His stake included 4.8 billion shares of SpaceX when the company went public earlier this year , an event that briefly made Musk the world's first trillionaire.
There are about 73 million children in the U.S., according to Census Bureau data .
Musk, the world's richest person, is currently worth about $904 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
Anthropic made its pledge to commit a portion of its shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, which it described as "a new entity," at a time when AI researchers from leading labs are warning of doomsday scenarios with potentially catastrophic outcomes that extend far beyond job losses.
Anthropic said the company has a two-pronged mission, with its research providing both a public benefit component and for-profit value. The new fund will give it more flexibility to make large donations to nonprofits or gifts to specific populations, the company added.
Anthropic also called out AI's impact on workers, acknowledging that tech advances could "cause instability" for many employees, and noted that it has already committed $200 million to analyzing and addressing AI's effects on parts of the labor force.
"Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good," Anthropic said.
Musk could conceivably use the recently created Trump Accounts program to gift SpaceX shares to U.S. children. The accounts, under new rules laid out by the Treasury, allow donors to deliver stock to the accounts without paying capital-gains taxes.
Michael Piwowar, executive director of Georgetown McDonough's Psaros Center for Financial Markets and Policy, called Trump Accounts the "perfect vehicle" through which Musk could deliver SpaceX shares to recipients.
"One of their great features, in addition to $1,000 seed money, is the ability of philanthropists to make philanthropic donations to a class of individuals," he said.
The Treasury Department is automatically enrolling up to 60 million children in the Trump Accounts program.
Piwowar added that with Musk's donation, "American children will immediately be invested in the American dream."
The tax-deferred accounts, created under Mr. Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill tax and spending bill for U.S. citizens born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028, are eligible for a $1,000 seed donation from the government.
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

Italy's government will dispatch 500 army troops to "defend Milan" after two days of unrest that saw demonstrators clash with police, loot shops and vandalise property.
The troop deployment, announced Monday by Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini, is expected to form part of a package of security measures to be approved at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
Luxury stores on Milan 's Via Montenapoleone cleared their windows Monday and shut early, bracing for a return of the violence that hit the city over the weekend.
Brands including Chanel, Tiffany and Dior took merchandise out of their displays as a precaution while police patrolled the street, where a handful of tourists looked on.
"From words to action: 500 more troops to defend Milan," Salvini, head of the co-ruling right-wing League party, wrote on social media.
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who faces a national election next year, condemned the violence. She chaired a meeting with ministers and security chiefs on Monday to discuss the situation.
"The government will respond firmly to these attacks on the state, including through measures aimed at curbing violence by minors," Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, who also serves as deputy prime minister like Salvini, wrote on X.
Corriere della Sera newspaper said Meloni was considering extending preventive detention for minors and cracking down on youth gangs as part of the planned crackdown. The measures would bring forward some provisions contained in an existing security bill currently being examined by parliament.
The weekend trouble began as an initially peaceful demonstration on Saturday over poor public services and rising costs. However, several hundred hooded protesters, many believed to be minors, then set bins ablaze and looted shops in the city centre.
Ransacked stores included sports retailers Decathlon and Arc'teryx and mobile phone operator Vodafone. Clothing brands Levi's and Under Armour, as well as Decathlon, covered their shop windows with cardboard and wooden panels in fear of more violence.
Italian police said officers detained 271 young people during unrest in Milan on Sunday. Of those taken to police stations, 32 were arrested, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, police said on Monday.
A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.
The unrest followed clashes on Saturday in Milan and other northern cities including Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, where 28 protesters were arrested, according to a police report released on Sunday.
The disturbances echoed unrest in neighbouring France , where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising living costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years.

articles.title_orig: Central NY paving giant closes in on $450 million sale to competitor
articles.title_zh: Central NY paving giant closes in on $450 million sale to competitor
articles.content_orig:
The Suit-Kote operation in Jamestown is up for sale as part of a plan to allow Suit-Kote to merge with Colas, a global road construction and maintenance company based in Paris, France and a subsidiary of the Bouygues Group.
Colas’ August stock purchase agreement with Suit-Kote, a Cortland-based company with a plant in Jamestown, has drawn the attention of the New York and Pennsylvania attorneys general.
Colas and Suit-Kote are two of the leading producers of asphalt emulsions and pavement preservation services in the northeast, including Pennsylvania. They use and sell asphalt emulsions to complete their own projects and sell and distribute these products to external customers. A proposed merger of the company, the attorneys general for New York and Pennsylvania say, would significantly increase concentration in already highly concentrated markets.
Asphalt emulsions are products made from bitumen or liquid asphalt, water and emulsifiers that are generally used in pavement preservation.
On Friday, David Sunday, Pennsylvania attorney general, asked a federal district court in Pennsylvania to rule the merger of Suit-Kote and Colas Inc. violates Section 7 of the federal Clayton Act and restrain Colas from carrying out the acquisition or any other agreement by which Colas will merge or acquire Suit-Kote. Colas purchased all of the outstanding shares of Suit-Kote in August.
The companies -- previously competitors -- produce and sell asphalt products and services in Pennsylvania to governmental entities (including PennDOT and municipalities) and commercial purchasers. The companies also offer pavement preservation services, such as chip sealing, micro-surfacing, milling, and other similar processes that maintain pavements including roads.
The Pennsylvania Attorney General's action prompted the companies to agree to divest four facilities, including one in Bloomsburg, where the companies also agreed to commit $6.5 million to build out that facility with an emulsion mill, storage for asphalt emulsions, and pavement preservation equipment. Doing so will allow the merger to move forward.
"This is a very important action taken by my Antitrust Team that will ensure a fair marketplace is maintained for these products and services," Attorney General Sunday said. "It will protect critical roadway infrastructure in central and western Pennsylvania and preserve the government funds that pay for it. The Antitrust Team engages in complicated work to make sure transactions between companies do not harm Pennsylvania, its economy, and its consumers."
The Pennsylvania Attorney General’s office wrote in its court filing late last week that Colas’ acquisition of Suit-Kote’s asphalt emulsions manufacturing and pavement preservation services will give Colas control over the supply of asphalt sold to the state of Pennsylvania and access to asphalt and pavement preservation that Pennsylvania municipalities need to complete road maintenance projects.
In order to resolve the Commonwealth’s concerns with their proposed transaction and preserve competition in the affected markets, Colas and Suit-Kote have agreed to divest four facilities to a qualified buyer: three Suit-Kote facilities in New York (Belmont, Buffalo and Jamestown) and one Colas facility in Pennsylvania (Bloomsburg). They have also agreed to invest up to $6.5 million to build out the Bloomsburg facility with an emulsion mill, adequate storage for asphalt emulsions, and pavement preservation equipment. Additionally, they have agreed to invest up to $3.5 million to build out the Belmont facility with pavement preservation equipment.
"No one should be forced to pay unfair prices for safe, well-maintained roads," said New York Attorney General Letitia James. "Protecting competition in this industry will ensure New Yorkers' tax dollars are spent fairly and asphalt companies will continue to provide high-quality services to our towns and counties."
Suit-Kote specializes in the distribution of liquid asphalt, in the manufacture of emulsion mixes, and in road construction and pavement preservation across multiple states in the northeastern United States. With over 750 employees, Suit-Kote generates approximately 500 million US dollars in revenue annually.
This acquisition is in line with the Colas strategy of pursuing its international growth in targeted areas (Northern Europe, United States, Germany and Australia). It will strengthen Colas’s positions in the industries of this highpotential country. In particular, it will help Colas Group to develop its business on the bitumen distribution market in the northeastern United States, according to a company news release in August.
“Suit-Kote’s regional roots, its expertise in bitumen processing and its model combining production, logistics and implementation will provide lasting support for our development in the United States”, says John Harrington, Colas executive vice president for the United States.
Colas has been operating in North America for over 60 years. It employs 13,500 people and generated 28% of its revenue there at the end of 2024, making it the Group’s second-largest market after France.

articles.title_orig: Unverified claims say Kim Jong Un is in a coma after brain hemorrhage
articles.title_zh: Unverified claims say Kim Jong Un is in a coma after brain hemorrhage
articles.content_orig:
U nverified claims circulating on social media say North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is in a coma after suffering a brain hemorrhage, prompting analysts to watch Pyongyang for either a show of public mourning or evidence that he is alive and well.
The claims, which have not been confirmed, say K im was rushed out of North Korea for emergency treatment because of what online users describe as poor medical facilities in Pyongyang. According to the speculation, he was taken to Peking Union Medical College in Beijing.
Kim was last seen in public on October 11, when he toured a new defense museum at an undisclosed location in Pyongyang. His 13-year-old daughter, Kim Ju Ae, accompanied him, according to photographs from the visit.
Benedict Rogers, a North Korea analyst, said he expected the government to release evidence of Kim’s well-being in response to the rumors. Speaking to The Sun’s YouTube channel, From The Newsroom, he noted that similar stories have surfaced before.
“He doesn’t look a well man,” Rogers said, adding that the leader is “extremely overweight.”
Rogers said that when a North Korean supreme leader has died in the past, the state has staged an “orchestrated outpouring of public grief,” with crowds wailing in the streets and newsreaders appearing visibly emotional. No such scenes have emerged, he said. Either they will, he suggested, or, if Kim is alive, the authorities will release proof.
Rumors about Kim’s health are not new. In 2020, a wave of social media speculation claimed he had died after he disappeared from public view for several months. During that episode, a former diplomat claimed Kim was in a coma and ready to hand power to his sister, Kim Yo Jong.
Experts say Kim Yo Jong, 38, who already wields significant influence within the nuclear-armed government, would take the reins if her brother died. Analysts believe she would serve as an interim leader until Kim Ju Ae is old enough to lead.
On Monday, Kim Yo Jong said Pyongyang was considering deploying additional tactical weapons near the border with South Korea.
South Korean intelligence officials have long said Kim Ju Ae is her father’s heir apparent, though she has not been officially named his successor.
She made her first public appearance in November 2022 at a missile launch, and she accompanied her father on a state visit to China last year. If she ever took power, she would be the first woman to lead North Korea in its dynastic history.
One insider told The Sun that as the daughter of the leader, she would be expected to play “the bloodsport of politics,” which would require removing disloyal aides “through violent means.”
Earlier this month, reports citing South Korea’s National Intelligence Service said Kim’s diet of steak and lobster had left him “extremely obese.”
The agency said he weighs more than 310 pounds (140 kilograms) at 5 feet 7 inches tall, a level that puts him at serious risk of cardiovascular disease. His heavy smoking has also raised questions about who would succeed him.
Kim took power after the death of his father, Kim Jong Il, who ruled from 1994 until 2011. In 2013, Kim had his uncle, Jang Song Thaek, executed by firing squad.

articles.title_orig: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
articles.title_zh: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
articles.content_orig:
Open source Windows alternative ReactOS has reached a major milestone: The operating system can now be installed directly onto an NT Files System drive partition. As reported by Phoronix , the move to NTFS clears a long-standing hurdle for the project and brings it one step closer to finally reaching beta.
Prior to this latest announcement, ReactOS required users to keep a FAT32 partition for installations. A proprietary Microsoft-developed filesystem, NTFS can trace its roots back through the Windows NT family lineage starting in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1. The variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001 remains the standard used by most Windows systems today. With ReactOS’s stated goal of reaching binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, being confined to FAT32 partitions was a practical barrier to clear on the way to reproducing the Windows environment.
However, users looking to hop off the Windows train shouldn’t be grabbing their bags just yet. ReactOS wrote that the new driver still “lacks caching (which causes inferior performance), journaling and security support.” So while the new driver is here, even the most intrepid of OS tinkerers should tread carefully. The ReactOS team warned in its announcement on X that there are still “potentially undiscovered bugs.”
The new driver closes a gap in development of nearly a decade. Read-only NTFS support was added to ReactOS all the way back in 2016, with boot support landing on FreeLoader in 2022. That meant that ReactOS’s bootloader could read from an NTFS partition, but the OS was unable to be directly installed there.
ReactOS is a community-developed open source project that describes itself as “mostly driven by volunteers.” Development is coordinated through public channels like GitHub and the project’s forums . Those who might be interested in lending a hand to ReactOS’s development can visit the project website to learn more about how to contribute . The project’s decades-long timeline underscores the scope and difficulty of reimplementing an operating system from scratch, and why the project has remained in alpha for so long.
The ReactOS project may never be a truly viable alternative to Windows for most users, but this step forward means that at least now it can be installed on the same filesystem as the real thing.

articles.title_orig: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.title_zh: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
articles.content_orig:
The fire that killed four members of the Canadian military and injured dozens of others on Saturday spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.
It broke out in a grassy training area at a base in the province of Alberta and spread rapidly due to strong winds.
"The fire was 1km (0.6 miles) away when the wind shifted," said Maj-Gen Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division of the Canadian Armed Forces. "It is not normal for a fire to move a kilometre in 30 to 60 seconds."
Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime". Officials have ruled out the possibility of "any terrorist activity".
Speaking in the House of Commons on Monday, Carney said the fire was "driven by ferocious winds".
"The fire jumped nearly a kilometer less than a minute to where the soldiers were gathered," he said, adding that the cause of the fire was not yet known.
Carney said the injuries occurred "in the space of a few minutes".
The blaze began at about 16:00 (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases.
The BBC has confirmed that Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark have died.
Of the 39 injured people receiving care in hospital, at least 19 are in a critical condition.
Warren Thirsk, an emergency department doctor at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, told Canadian broadcaster CBC that the number of patients involved in the incident had "completely overwhelmed" healthcare facilities in Wainwright.
Tributes are being paid to the servicemen who died.
Patricia Farrell, the mother of Shaun Farrell, wrote on Facebook that it was "with heavy hearts that we share the news that our son, Shaun Farrell, has passed away to be with our Heavenly Father".
Wong received a tribute from the Loyal Edmonton Regiment, of which he was part. The regiment was "deeply saddened", it wrote in a Facebook post of its own. It sent "heartfelt condolences to [the group's] families, friends, and fellow soldiers".
The mother of Goulding, Sonia Monk, said her late son was an exceptional athlete and a natural leader. "He was always the guy who kept everybody's spirits up," she told CBC. "He really was the light of my life."
Canadian PM Carney said on Monday that Goulding was known as "a generous and deeply loyal friend".
Lykkemark, Carney said, "was known for his gift for lightening a hard day, his quick wit - he dreamed of a career in law enforcement".
"These were sons, brothers, partners, friends, young men with bright futures who chose to serve our country and who died in that cause," Carney said.
In recounting Saturday's events, Rutland told reporters that members of the infantry had been conducting "high-intensity combat training with live munitions" at a grenade range and attack range.
He told reporters that officials knew about the fire on the base for several hours, but it was decided that training "could carry on for a certain amount of time".
"I spoke to my commander last night, and he said within 30 seconds to a minute they saw no fire, and then there was a fire right on top of them," Rutland said.
Rutland said it was not yet known what exactly caused the fire.
Some witnesses had said they had heard explosions, fuelling speculation that oil and gas infrastructure may have been hit and sparked the fire. But Rutland said authorities "do not believe this [incident] to be a result of any oil and gas infrastructure".
The Canadian Armed Forces has said that "while the incident remains under investigation, at this time, there are no indications that it was the result of any terrorist activity".
Forecasters had issued a wind warning on Saturday for large parts of Alberta, predicting wind gusts of up to 90km/h (66mph), Canadian broadcaster CBS said.
According to Rutland, the investigation may take at least a month.
Wainwright, about 130 miles east of Edmonton, Alberta's capital, is one of the main bases used by the Canadian military for live-fire training exercises, and it houses troops from Canada and allied countries.
About 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers are on site on a typical day.

The US State Department has added a “wrongful detention” warning to its travel advisory for China, alerting Americans to the risk of being detained arbitrarily under Chinese law.
On Monday, the official China travel advisory added the “D” risk indicator for wrongful detention, while maintaining the country’s overall advisory level at Level 2, or “Exercise Increased Caution”.
The advisory urges Americans travelling to mainland China to exercise caution due to the “arbitrary enforcement of local laws, the use of exit bans without a fair and transparent process under the law, and the risk of wrongful detention”.
The move comes as Washington and Beijing seek to maintain an improving bilateral relationship following a warm welcome for Chinese President Xi Jinping by US President Donald Trump during the September visit to Washington. The two leaders are expected to meet twice more this year.

articles.title_orig: We Might Finally Know What's Written On That Mysterious Plaque In Super Mario 64
articles.title_zh: We Might Finally Know What's Written On That Mysterious Plaque In Super Mario 64
articles.content_orig:
The plaque's message has haunted the internet for 30 years.
Super Mario 64 fans have been obsessing over a blurry plaque in the castle courtyard for over 30 years. We might finally know what's written on it, according to a report by Video Games Chronicle . This is thanks to a programmer who used open-source computational analysis software to get to the bottom of things.
This isn't graphical upscaling software. The image is simply too blurry for that. Even modern reissues still have that same blurry plaque, so that hasn't been a help to anyone.
Instead, programmer Mochi64 used the analysis engine to pore through millions of combinations of words and fonts, looking for something that matched the pixels in the plaque. The end result? Mochi64 believes the top of the plaque reads "Eternal Star" and the bottom reads "We hope so."
This isn't an absolute answer. Those are simply the two sentences that provided the closest possible match via the analysis software. There's still a chance it could be something else, but the software did make millions of comparisons.
There were several high-profile rumors throughout the 1990s and beyond that the plaque read "L is Real 2401." This was seen as a tease that Luigi was hiding somewhere in the game. IGN actually offered a $100 bounty to anyone who could figure out how to unlock Luigi and Nintendo Power even mentioned the "L is Real 2401" theory in an April Fool's Day issue.
Here's your only official footage of multiplayer Super Mario 64 from a Spaceworld 95 video kiosk as the camera clearly focuses on both characters https://t.co/cLCdSIl5B9 pic.twitter.com/RdtTGb8LpJ
— Yakumono (@LuigiBlood) December 15, 2023
This rumor was given new life when the game's director, Shigeru Miyamoto, noted that the team had been experimenting with a two-player mode. He also said that they gave up on the idea to conserve memory, but that didn't stop the rumor mill. An early build showing Mario and Luigi running around a bare room didn't help things.
So there you have it. The phrase "Eternal Star" makes sense, as the plaque sits below a giant star statue . Perhaps the second sentence of "We hope so" indicates that the developers wanted players to collect every star. In any event, it's highly unlikely we'll ever get official confirmation from Nintendo.

articles.title_orig: United Airlines adds 5 nonstop routes to its lineup — including new international destinations
articles.title_zh: United Airlines adds 5 nonstop routes to its lineup — including new international destinations
articles.content_orig:
United Airlines is adding a few new destinations to its friendly skies roster.
The airline announced this week that it will add five new nonstop North American routes, with three serving cities north of the border.
Of the new routes, three will be international expansions, and two will be domestic.
Experts say the domestic routes between Houston, TX and Joplin, MO, and between Washington Dulles and Lancaster, PA, stem from ongoing construction and subsequent operational restrictions at Chicago O’Hare International.
Meanwhile, the international additions of Denver to Ottawa, Denver to Quebec City, and Newark to St. John’s reflect the recent transborder business agreement between United and Air Canada.
Some of these Canadian routes are a welcome return while others mark the establishment of a completely new connection.
The Denver-to-Ottawa service re-establishes a former United Airlines route discontinued in 2010, alongside a fresh link between Denver and Quebec City.
Additionally, United will return to Newfoundland and Labrador for the first time since 2016 with seasonal flights connecting Newark and St. John’s.
Domestic service will begin this spring while the Canadian connections take flight this summer.
Meanwhile, to complement these additions, Air Canada is offering new connections between Toronto and Louisville and Quebec and Indianapolis, with seasonal service expected to run June through September of next year.
Air Canada is also taking off with new flights between Edmonton and Newark.
According to Bloomberg, United and Air Canada are looking to add as many as 10 additional US-Canada itineraries
“Air Canada and United’s long-standing partnership continues to deliver meaningful results for our customers and communities. For nearly three decades, Air Canada and United have worked to facilitate seamless travel and strengthen connectivity between Canada and the United States,” said Mark Galardo, Executive Vice President & Chief Commercial Officer and President, Cargo at Air Canada, on October 16 .
The added routes come amid a slew of other switches United Airlines has made of late.
Earlier this month, United launched a cheaper first-class fare .
Back in February, United quietly updated a noise policy that — before the change — had flyers nearly losing their minds .
The 100-year-old company told The Post it has started forcing passengers to wear headphones when listening to content on phones, tablets or anything that makes sound.
United’s Contract of Carriage — a rules and policy handbook — was updated on February 27 to add the new “headphone language.”
More recently, the “friendliness” of United’s skies was put in peril when a Russian woman was accused of biting and kicking  United flight attendants during a booze-fueled midair meltdown.

articles.title_orig: From France to Albania, social unrest is setting Europe’s streets ablaze
articles.title_zh: From France to Albania, social unrest is setting Europe’s streets ablaze
articles.content_orig:
Student protests in France are into their second month , escalating into demonstrations across Europe.
What began in September in France with pupils protesting against overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages has grown into wider anger at the cost of living and planned cuts to public services.
Protesters in Albania, Belgium, Greece, Italy, Portugal and Spain have also taken to the streets over the lack of affordable housing, rising costs and failing public services – with many young people saying they no longer expect to be better off than their parents.
Facing their anger are leaders such as French President Emmanuel Macron , Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Spain’s PM Pedro Sanchez and Portugal’s PM Luis Montenegro. Sanchez belongs to the left, Meloni to the right and Macron and Montenegro are conservative-leaning centrists. But while their politics vary, they all face mounting unrest because of soaring costs of living.
Are they out of touch with the experiences and sentiments of youth in their countries? Al Jazeera visualises how prices, wages, housing and education have changed in France, Italy, Spain and Portugal over the past 26 years, from when Macron, Meloni, Sanchez and Montenegro were in their 20s, much like many of the protesters angry with them.
The prices paid for everyday items such as food, energy, transport and bills have risen by between 59 and 78 percent since 2000 in France, Italy, Spain and Portugal, according to Eurostat – the European Union’s statistics agency. Its harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP) is the EU’s official measure of how much everyday goods and services cost.
Spain recorded the steepest increase at 78 percent, followed by Portugal at 71 percent, 68 percent in Italy and France at 59 percent.
That means goods and services that cost 100 euros ($112) in 2000 now cost about 178 euros ($200) in Spain, 171 euros ($192) in Portugal, 168 euros ($188) in Italy and 159 euros ($178) in France.
Prices rose by about 2 percent a year on average, but jumped in 2022, when annual inflation hit 8.7 percent in Italy, 8.3 percent in Spain, 8.1 percent in Portugal and 5.9 percent in France, the highest rate in all four countries since at least 2000.
The surge was driven mainly by energy costs, which soared after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. By October that year, eight months into the war, energy prices across the eurozone were almost 42 percent higher than a year earlier, and food prices were also rising sharply, according to Eurostat .
Between 2021 and 2023, prices increased by 12 to 15 per cent in the four countries. Wages failed to keep up, and because prices do not fall back once inflation eases, many households are still feeling the squeeze today.
Once inflation is taken into account, the average full-time wage in Italy fell by almost 5 per cent between 2000 and 2025. Over the same period, real wages rose by 7 per cent in Spain, 11 per cent in France and 20 per cent in Portugal, according to OECD wage data adjusted with Eurostat’s price index.
In Spain most new jobs were in tourism and services, and were often seasonal and poorly paid,  Jaime Velazquez, a journalist in Madrid, told Al Jazeera’s Inside Story .
Julius Fintelmann, cofounder and editor-in-chief of The European Correspondent, said ageing societies were squeezing out opportunities for younger workers, adding that the pay gap between older and younger workers has been widening across high-income economies for decades, so the promise that each generation would be better off than the last no longer holds.
Housing has become harder to afford in all four countries since 2000, according to the OECD’s price-to-income ratio. It provides a broad picture of how house prices have changed relative to incomes over time. When prices rise faster than incomes, the ratio goes up, suggesting homes are becoming less affordable on average.
However, it doesn’t show which households or regions are hit hardest, does not account for mortgage and borrowing costs, and says nothing about the quality of the homes people are paying for.
Spain has seen the biggest change. Its price-to-income ratio is 56 per cent higher than in 2000, even after falling sharply following the 2008 financial crisis.
In France, the ratio is 39 per cent higher than in 2000, though it has eased slightly since peaking in 2022.
Italy is the exception where house prices have broadly kept pace with incomes, leaving the ratio just 5 per cent higher than in 2000.
Portugal has seen the sharpest change in recent years. Its price-to-income ratio fell steadily for 15 years after 2000, meaning homes became more affordable. But since 2015 the ratio has risen by 67 per cent.
The OECD publishes the price-to-income ratio with 2015 as its reference year. To compare it with the wage and price data in this article, which started in 2000, Al Jazeera has reset the figures so that 2000 = 100.
Education has been at the heart of the unrest in France, where protests began because of overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages. While in Belgium and Albania, demonstrators have rallied against the rising cost of education and access to universities.
According to the latest data from Eurostat , France’s public spending on education amounts to 5.1 per cent of its gross domestic product (GDP) compared to 5.6 per cent in 2000.
Italy spent 4.4 per cent of its GDP on education compared to 4 per cent in 2024, Spain spent 4.1 per cent in 2000 and the same in 2024. Portugal spent 4.8 per cent in 2000 and 4.3 per cent in 2024.

articles.title_orig: Violence, looting, arson: France faces an ominous doom loop
articles.title_zh: Violence, looting, arson: France faces an ominous doom loop
articles.content_orig:
Social unrest , political instability and mounting national debt weighed on French assets on Monday, with government bonds and Paris-listed stocks under pressure.
The euro was last seen down 0.15% against the U.S. dollar, and was 0.1% lower against the British pound.
The French 10-year bond yield jumped more than 10 basis points, taking it just shy of its highest level in decades. Higher yields represent higher borrowing costs for the government in the debt market. The country's 2-year and 30-year yields were up 6 basis points and 8 basis points, respectively.
Stocks are also feeling the heat, with the CAC 40 index down 1.7% in afternoon deals on Monday. The market has significantly underperformed its European peers in recent years as political volatility has mounted — despite only around 15% of its revenues being generated domestically — with banks under particular pressure.
The French stock market is historically sensitive to any widening in the so-called "OAT-Bund spread", the extra bond yield France pays over Germany, which has hit the highest level since the European Sovereign Debt Crisis of the early 2010s. French yields now also surpass those of Italy or Greece, implying higher risk.
Widening bond spreads raise concerns about the cost for companies to raise capital and heighten fears of higher taxes and tighter regulation. The French stock market has also struggled due to the dominance of its luxury firms, which are suffering from a downturn in high-end Chinese consumer spending.
Hundreds of thousands of people marched over the weekend in protest over political paralysis , the cost of living and the state of public services, including schools and healthcare.
Mass gatherings in cities from Paris to Lyon and Marseille spilled into dramatic scenes of buildings and cars set on fire, clashes with police and more than 2,000 arrests.
"If you're an international investor thinking about whether you want to invest in French bonds, it's not helpful," Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday.
"It looks like either the bond markets riot, or the people riot, or both," Bell said.
Overseas investors hold a growing share of French debt, rising from around 48% at the start of 2022 to nearly 60% at the start of 2026, potentially meaning higher volatility in the bond market in a risk-off environment .
"What's needed in France is to get the fiscal position in order, they need to raise the retirement age — you can't retire at 62 if the average person's living to 84 — but if this is going on even before they start talking about that, then imagine what would happen on the streets of France if you tried to raise the retirement age to... I mean here in the U.K. it's 68," Bell added.
"It doesn't make the country look that governable against a time when they need to be putting through hard choices."
France's benchmark borrowing costs are touching their highest level since 2002, with investors demanding greater returns to lend to the government.
Key concerns include uncertainty over next year's presidential election, in which far-right Marine Le Pen is topping many polls , and whether the minority government of Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu can pass the 2027 budget currently under negotiation.
Budget negotiations are increasingly fraught in France and have toppled two of Lecornu's recent predecessors in recent years.
Analysts say lenders want a credible fiscal-consolidation plan to keep France from being caught in a debt spiral: weak growth and a persistently high deficit-to-GDP ratio are pushing up bond yields, raising the government's debt-servicing bill and widening the deficit further — which could drive borrowing costs higher still.
"It will be difficult to see the budget deficit come down without painful measures," Sharon Bell, senior European equity strategist at Goldman Sachs, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday.
"Taxes could well go up for French businesses. I think taxes may generally go up in France, fiscal consolidation means you need to either spend less or tax more. Those things are very tricky."
"Le Pen, who is riding high in the polls at the moment, she's talked about keeping a Golden Budget [rule] during her term, but she's not really detailed how that would happen," Bell continued.
"One of the reasons that OAT-Bund spreads are not coming in is because investors are skeptical that you will see any fiscal consolidation and a decline in that budget deficit."
But Ken Egan, senior director of sovereigns at ratings agency KBRA, noted auctions last week showed there remains "still very solid underlying demand for French debt."
"It is a more risk-off morning generally, but France is clearly taking a little more of the pressure... The question markets will be asking is how easily France can actually make progress from here," Egan said by email.
Goldman Sachs' Sharon Bell added that she did not believe current conditions warranted any emergency intervention by the European Central Bank, which "doesn't want" to use tools such as its Transmission Protection Instrument .
However, she said if spreads start to disrupt market liquidity, the ECB would opt to use the mechanism.
Such a move would be politically sensitive, likely requiring France to engage in even more stringent fiscal reforms over a long period akin to those by countries such as Greece, Portugal and Ireland during the euro area crisis, she added.
"Sometimes it does take market pressure, and that's what we've seen this year."
RBC BlueBay Asset Management's Mike Bell meanwhile said France was facing a "very real risk" of its own sovereign debt crisis.
"Ultimately they need to get the fiscal house in order. If you even suggested what's actually needed for that, you wouldn't get elected, and if you tried to put it in without having put it through on a mandate for election, then you'd have riots in the street."
Before any intervention, there will be an "almighty clash between whoever wins the next election" and the ECB, Bell added. The central bank is unlikely to step in unless countries comply with its excess deficit procedure, which states that the general government budget deficit must not exceed 3% of GDP. France's current deficit is around 5%.
Banque de France Governor Emmanuel Moulin told CNBC last week that rising French yields were due to political uncertainty, but said it was "possible to get back to a 3% deficit in 2029, which is the objective of the government."

For a limited time, the iPhone Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro Max will be limited to customers with a pickup reservation at Apple Stores in Japan and South Korea , according to notices posted on Apple's localized websites for those countries.
The notices suggest that the iPhone Duo will not be available for walk-in customers at Apple's retail locations in Japan and South Korea when the device launches on Friday, October 23, likely due to a mix of supply constraints and Apple's usual anti-scalping measures in Asia. It is unclear if this policy will extend to any other countries.
iPhone Duo pre-orders began on Friday , with shipping estimates on Apple's online store for newly-placed orders getting pushed back to January 25 within the first 30 minutes of pre-orders starting. In a statement issued later on Friday, Apple said demand for the iPhone Duo was " nothing short of extraordinary " and that it was "working hard" to fulfill orders "as quickly as possible." Apple did not disclose any specific sales figures.
Apple's online store says customers interested in reserving the iPhone Duo for Apple Store pickup should check back on Saturday, October 24 for more information.
iPhone Duo should be on display at Apple Stores around the world starting on Friday, October 23, but it is still not entirely clear if the device will be available for walk-in customers in the U.S. or any other countries, excluding Japan and South Korea. Our own Hartley Charlton reported that some Apple Store managers advised employees to warn customers against attempting to purchase the iPhone Duo on a walk-in basis at launch, but this was not companywide communication and Apple has yet to publicly comment on the matter.
It seems safe to say that even if some Apple Stores do have the iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, inventory will be extremely limited at first.

articles.title_zh: Toyota’s best-selling Corolla is going electric, and it will be made in China
articles.content_orig:
Toyota will produce the Corolla EV in China starting in 2028, alongside hybrid and gas-powered versions.
Since it went on sale in 1966, Toyota has sold over 57 million Corollas worldwide, making it the brand’s best-selling vehicle of all time.
Like the Prius, Toyota’s compact car attracted drivers with an affordable price and reputation as a reliable daily driver.
After 12 model changes, the next-generation Toyota Corolla is set for its biggest transformation to date.
Toyota revealed the next-gen Corolla Concept for the first time at the Japan Mobility Show almost a year ago. In addition to a pure electric version, former president and current CEO Koji Sato said the compact car would remain “a car for everyone,” with multiple powertrain options, including hybrid and gas-powered.
“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s CEO said at the time.
According to Nikkei, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.
The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrain options.
Toyota already uses the platform for several models, including under its luxury Lexus brand. By building the new Corolla in China, Toyota is expected to cut costs while speeding up development and output.
In addition to new longer-range electric vehicles, Toyota plans to build extended-range EVs under Lexus in China starting next year.
Toyota has yet to reveal any battery, powertrain specs, or other details. The next-gen Corolla is expected to remain close to the concept with a sleek, almost sports-car-like design. Aside from the huge COROLLA badge on the rear, you can barely tell it’s a Corolla.
In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company is being forced to adapt, or “it cannot survive,” amid new competition and technology from China.
The special broadcast went behind the scenes at the “top secret” next-gen Corolla development site.
During the broadcast, several Corolla Concept body types , including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were shown blurred in the background.
The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.
The hybrid will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.
Whether or not Toyota will bring the Corolla EV to the US is still unclear. Toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year.
According to Car and Driver , the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.
While the Corolla is still a top seller, it has lost some of its charm as newer vehicles arrive that are more advanced, more efficient, and better looking.
It’s about time for an overhaul. In China, Toyota’s sales dropped by 23%, marking the seventh straight month of lower sales due to weak demand for gas and hybrid models amid soaring fuel prices.
Toyota is restructuring its two joint ventures , FAW Toyota and GAC Toyota, to streamline operations and introduce more advanced tech in China.

articles.title_orig: Israeli police arrest 10 in connection with West Bank assaults
articles.title_zh: Israeli police arrest 10 in connection with West Bank assaults
articles.content_orig:
Amid US pressure on a surge of settler violence in the occupied West Bank, Israeli police arrested at least 10 suspects in the weekend attacks on a Washington Post journalist and an entourage of European diplomats.
Police said the operation to locate and arrest the suspects was called “Olive Leaf,” an apparent reference to the recent start of the olive harvest in the West Bank, which has seen a dramatic rise in settler attacks.
On Friday, settlers attacked and hospitalized veteran Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine as she traveled with a group of Palestinians at the start of the olive harvest. One day later, settlers attacked a group of European diplomats visiting the Palestinian Christian town of Taybeh.
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee welcomed the arrests as a “very positive development in finding & punishing those who severely attacked and beat Heidi Levine.”
According to police, security forces worked with the Israeli military to locate and arrest the suspects across the area with the attacks took place. “During this activity, 10 suspects were arrested, findings linking them to the incidents were sized and several vehicles were confiscated,” police said.
“We are working to collect evidence, findings and testimonies and to consolidate an evidentiary infrastructure that will enable bringing those involved to justice,” said Israel Police Superintendent Moshe Pinchi in a statement.
Israeli human rights group Yesh Din documented more than 530 incidents of settler violence since the beginning of the olive harvest in late-September, averaging 27 violent incidents each day. According to Yesh Din, Israeli soldiers were present at roughly one quarter of the attacks over this period.
On Saturday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Trump administration has told Israel that the US “doesn’t want to see a new spark” in the West Bank and called on Israel to take action against settler violence.
“We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff,” said Rubio before his flight to India and Uzbekistan. “The President has been very clear. He’s said this repeatedly. He does not want to see friction or anything - a crisis - going on in the West Bank.”
Despite video of the attacks on both Levine, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has tried to cast doubt on the violence, saying afterwards that “serious questions remain.” In an apparent attempt to avoid upsetting his right-wing voter base so close to Israel’s elections, Netanyahu has repeatedly downplayed the severity and scale of settler violence, claiming it’s carried out by a rogue group.
Meanwhile, Israel’s defense minister said on Monday he would not reinstate administrative detention against Jewish Israelis, which allows authorities to hold suspects without charge or trial. The draconian measure was one of Israel’s most effective tools against settler extremism, but the defense minister cancelled its use against Jewish Israelis as one of his first decisions nearly two years ago.
On Sunday, President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu ahead of the election, which will take place on October 27, calling him “Strong, Brave, and Brilliant.” For weeks, Trump had sidestepped questions on whether Netanyahu should be re-elected, including just days earlier when he said, “I don’t trust anyone in the world of politics.”

articles.title_orig: Something shifted in the housing market, and sellers felt it first
articles.title_zh: Something shifted in the housing market, and sellers felt it first
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
For most of the past decade, sellers named the terms, and buyers scrambled to meet them.
That arrangement is coming apart, and one of the clearest signs is who now pays to make a buyer's loan cheaper. Home sellers gave concessions in 44.7% of U.S. sales in August, the highest share for that month since at least 2020, according to Fortune .
Money got more expensive, and buyers felt it fast. With rates climbing well above 7%, a seller who chips in on the loan can actually do more for a buyer's budget than a small trim to the asking price.
Also read: Jeff Bezos has a blunt answer for why housing is so expensive
Freddie Mac's weekly survey tells the same story. The average 30-year fixed rate held at 7.40% as of Oct. 15, compared with 6.27% a year earlier, Freddie Mac reported .
That gap of more than a full percentage point has reshaped what a typical household can afford, leaving many would-be buyers on the sidelines.
Fewer people are even applying. Mortgage applications dropped in the week ending Oct. 9 as rates pushed higher, and purchase loans fell right along with refinancing. More borrowers have also opted for adjustable-rate loans, pushing that share to its highest since October 2025.
The monthly cost of that climb is easy to see. Senate Banking Committee staff for Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) estimated that a typical buyer now pays about $361 more a month than in late February, TheStreet reported .
Sellers are adjusting their asking prices, too. A record September share of active listings had a price cut in the four weeks ending Sept. 20, according to TheStreet , which reviewed Redfin's data.
Denver led the major metros for cuts, while San Francisco, buoyed by wealth from the AI boom, posted the smallest share.
Here is how it plays out at the closing table. A lump sum goes to the lender up front, and the borrower gets a lower rate in return, sometimes only for the first year or two and sometimes for the life of the loan.
If the seller writes that check, the buyer's payment shrinks, and the buyer never pays for the discount.
There is a tradeoff buyers should understand before signing. A seller-funded buydown does not lower the agreed purchase price. Compared with a deal struck at a lower price, the buyer walks away with a smaller payment but starts out owing more on the loan.
Redfin counts rate buydowns alongside money for repairs and closing costs when it tracks seller concessions. Roughly 15.8% of homes sold in August came with a price drop in addition to a concession, a record for that month. In other words, a meaningful slice of buyers is now getting help on both fronts.
Experienced sellers are building that help into their math before a sign goes up. New Orleans investor Dominique Gunderson plans each flip around a sale price that already assumes two price cuts and a $10,000 closing-cost concession.
She said on the BiggerPockets podcast that today's buyers have become extremely picky about price and finishes.
Homebuilders have leaned on these tools for well over a year. In July, more than a third of builders cut prices and nearly two-thirds offered sales incentives to keep transactions moving forward, a measure that has stayed above 60% for 16 straight months, TheStreet reported , citing National Association of Home Builders survey data.
Those deals put real pressure on resale owners nearby. Builder buydowns and closing-cost credits can push the monthly cost of a new home below that of a comparable existing house, and most individual sellers lack the financial margin to match a full builder package.
Goldman Sachs rethinks U.S. economy as interest rates stay higher
Heating bills expected to jump by $1,000 in some U.S. states this winter
How stocks will react when the catalysts are few
Even generous incentives have not fixed weak demand. Builders sold fewer new homes in the first half of 2026 than in any comparable stretch since 2017, Zillow found, according to TheStreet . Zillow senior economist Orphe Divounguy pointed to higher mortgage rates, softer hiring and sticky inflation as the main drags on household formation.
Agents say buyers have noticed the shift and are pressing their advantage. A Dallas-based Redfin agent said house hunters are asking for every concession they can think of, especially on newly built homes, as reported by Redfin . Eight of the 10 metros where concessions are most common sit in the Sun Belt.
Buyers hoping to simply wait out high rates may be disappointed. Fannie Mae's October forecast calls for the 30-year rate to average 7.4% in the fourth quarter of 2026 and 7.5% through 2027, while the Mortgage Bankers Association expects slightly lower readings that still stay above 7%.
That outlook makes negotiating skill more valuable than timing. Redfin senior economist Asad Khan said the sellers moving homes quickly are getting savvier about pricing right from day one . Redfin also noted that homes sitting on the market for more than a month may justify offers below asking.
The next big test comes at the Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Oct. 27 and 28, which could move Treasury yields and the mortgage quotes tied to them. Until borrowing costs ease, a seller-paid buydown may remain the quickest path to a payment buyers can live with.
